records.people: Burkhard Balz (Member of the Executive Board of the Deutsche Bundesbank since 1 September 2018)
records.move: from twenty years at Commerzbank AG, latterly head of department for institutional clients in Hanover (2004-2009), to the Executive Board of the Deutsche Bundesbank (from 1 September 2018)
records.summary: The Bundesbank's own curriculum vitae for Executive Board member Burkhard Balz records a career at Commerzbank AG: trained as a bank clerk in Hanover 1989-1991, a corporate-banking traineeship 2000-2001, desk officer at the bank's liaison office to the European Union in Brussels 2001-2002, corporate customer adviser 2002-2004 and head of department for institutional clients in Hanover 2004-2009, before a term as a Member of the European Parliament and his appointment to the Executive Board on 1 September 2018. Ownership evidence: the Bundesbank page states the employment only and says nothing about who owns Commerzbank AG; Commerzbank is already carried on this map as a private-finance employer from the Weidmann record for the same country, and is a listed commercial bank.
records.source_title: Burkhard Balz, Member of the Executive Board of the Deutsche Bundesbank (Deutsche Bundesbank)

records.summary: The Banca d'Italia's own notice on the death of Fabrizio Saccomanni sets out his whole career at the bank: he joined in June 1967, was seconded to the International Monetary Fund from 1970 to 1975, became head of the foreign relations service in 1984 and central director for foreign activities in 1997, left in 2003 for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and returned in 2006 as Director General, remaining honorary Director General from 2014. The same notice records that from April 2018 he was chairman of the board of directors of UniCredit. Ownership evidence: the Banca d'Italia notice states the chairmanship but not the ownership of UniCredit; UniCredit S.p.A. is a listed commercial bank already carried on this map as a party. This is a different person, employer and decade from the Draghi records the map holds for Italy.

blanks.note: BEL, refused on the ownership test alone, and the career half is solid, so the next round should not re-chase the career. The National Bank of Belgium's own press release of 29 April 2009 on the death of Governor Emeritus Baron Jean Godeaux (https://www.nbb.be/doc/ts/enterprise/press/2009/cp20090429fr.pdf) gives a full dated career: he joined the Bank's foreign department in 1947, held posts at the IMF and the IBRD from 1949 to 1954, and on returning to Belgium in 1955 - 'Monsieur Godeaux entama une carriere a la Banque Lambert' - of which he became chairman of the management board in 1973; he chaired the Banking Commission from 1974 to 1982 and was appointed Governor on 1 March 1982 ('Le 1er mars 1982, Monsieur Godeaux fut nomme gouverneur de la Banque'), retiring in July 1989. The release was read for the ownership words and uses neither 'banque privee' nor 'prive' and names no shareholder or owner of Banque Lambert, so the move cannot be counted as private under this row's rule. A source that states Banque Lambert's ownership - a Lambert-family or Groupe Bruxelles Lambert structure document - would convert this in one fetch.

AUT: the obvious career-list vein at the central bank is empty. The Oesterreichische Nationalbank's Corporate Governance Bericht 2025 (https://www.oenb.at/dam/jcr:77307c01-f0f8-4761-9965-5ed4a20d857b/corporate_governance_bericht_2025.pdf) was downloaded and fully extracted; section 3.1 'Darstellung des Direktoriums' gives the Direktorium members' names, birth years and the dates of their first and current appointments only, with no biography and no previous employer for any of them, and the following section 'Mitgliedschaften der einzelnen Mitglieder des Direktoriums in Organen anderer Unternehmen und Einrichtungen per 31. Dezember 2025' was read in full for Governor Martin Kocher, Vice-Governor Edeltraud Stiftinger and Direktor Josef Meichenitsch: every outside seat listed is at a public body or a state-owned company - BIS, the ECB Governing Council and its task forces, the ESRB, the IMF, the Finanzmarktaufsichtsbehorde, GELDSERVICE AUSTRIA, Oesterreichische Banknoten- und Sicherheitsdruck, IG Immobilien Invest, Bundestheater-Holding, WIFO and the Club of Rome - so there is no private-finance seat to record either. The OeNB's own corporate-governance report therefore carries no careers; the untried route for Austria is the board and supervisory-board biographies of the Austrian commercial banks (Erste Group, Raiffeisen Bank International, BAWAG, Oberbank), which publish fuller CVs than the central bank does.

PRT, refused on the no-dates rule and on part-duplication. Searching the career phrase in Portuguese produced one real candidate, the economist Teodora Cardoso: eco.sapo.pt's profile page (https://eco.sapo.pt/personalidade/teodora-cardoso/) says she was an economist at the Banco de Portugal for nearly two decades, headed its statistics and economic studies department, and was 'consultora da administracao e administradora entre 2008 e 2012', and also that she was 'consultora da administracao do BPI' - adviser to the board of BPI - with NO dates for the BPI role. That is exactly the case the brief says to hold: no years, and BPI's ownership changed over the relevant period. It is also the same employer as the record the map already holds for Portugal (Vitor Constancio at Banco Portugues de Investimento), so even dated it would be a weaker second instance of the same firm. The page is press, so it would in any case have been weak_source. Untried for Portugal: the board CV PDFs that Millennium bcp and Novo Banco publish for their own directors, which is where a dated Banco de Portugal-to-private move would be stated by the hiring firm.

GRC: the hiring-firm route was tried and the one Bank of Greece mention it produced is not a career move. Attica Bank's own published CVs of its candidate board members (https://www.crediabank.com/media/qhabnpna/attica-bank_viografika-simeiomata_ypopsifion-melon-ds-1.pdf, six pages, ten full biographies) were downloaded, extracted and searched for 'Trapeza tis Ellados': the only hit is Panayiotis Alexakis, who from 2017 sat on the selection committee of the Hellenic Financial Stability Fund 'os ekprosopos tis Trapezas tis Ellados' - as the Bank of Greece's representative - which is a delegated seat held on the central bank's behalf and not employment at a private firm; the second hit in the same document is a different person's service at the National Bank of Greece with no central bank in the career. A Greek-language search for the career phrase returned only appointment stories for the sitting deputy governor Dimitrios Tsomokos (an academic) and board changes at National Bank of Greece. Untried for Greece: the Bank of Greece's own past-governor and past-deputy-governor pages, and the board biographies of Alpha Bank, Eurobank and National Bank of Greece, each of which publishes fuller CVs than the central bank.

BRN: the one route round 68 recorded as not reached has now been read and it names no careers. The Brunei Darussalam Central Bank Annual Report 2025 (https://cms.bdcb.gov.bn/storage/uploads/publications/17824568929284490.pdf, downloaded, 302,000 characters extracted) carries a 'Report of the Board' whose 'Board of Directors' list gives each member's name and current public office and nothing else: Chairman Dato Seri Paduka Khairuddin bin Haji Abdul Hamid (Deputy Minister of Finance and Economy (Economy) 17 July 2022 - 8 August 2025, Ministry of Primary Resources and Tourism from 8 October 2025), Deputy Chairman Pengiran Datin Seri Paduka Zety Sufina (Deputy Minister of Finance and Economy (Fiscal)), the Deputy State Mufti, the Solicitor General, two Permanent Secretaries and Managing Director Rashidah binti Haji Sabtu. No previous employer, no private firm, no career line for any of them - it is the same ex officio arrangement the map already carries as an event for Brunei. With round 68's reading of Baiduri Bank's management-committee page and Baiduri's Corporate Governance Disclosure 2025, both of which were exhausted, Brunei now has the central bank's own newest annual report and the largest private bank's own leadership page read and no central-bank career anywhere. Remaining untried: the board or management pages of BIBD and the smaller Brunei banks and insurers.

DJI: the second of the three Djiboutian commercial banks named as the remaining route was opened and it carries careers but no central bank career. Salaam African Bank's own 'Our Leadership' page (https://www.banksalaam.com/?p=7729) names four directors - Ali Abdallah Hettam (Chairman), Abdirahman Mohamed Abdilahi, Abdulkadir Ali Hassan, Osman Doualeh Dirir - and five managers - Jama Hersi Abdi (General Manager), Ahmed Moallim Hersi, Abdalleh Said Waiss, Hamoud Djibril, Souleiman Hassan Ismail - and unlike Bank of Africa Mer Rouge it does publish previous employers: UKAP Holdings and Comad Group for the chairman, Red Sea Petroleum Company for Abdilahi, East Africa Bank 2009-2013 for Djibril, Almazeed Communication in Dubai for the general manager. Not one of them is described as having worked at the Banque Centrale de Djibouti; the only mention of the central bank on the page is that the bank 'is licensed and regulated by the Central Bank of Djibouti'. Djibouti now has three documents read with no career: the central bank's Rapport Annuel 2024 (round 68), Bank of Africa Mer Rouge's accounts (round 69) and this page. One route left: BCIMR, which publishes no leadership page that any search has returned.

ERI: unchanged, and the recommendation stands - reclassify as structurally closed rather than leave it as a target. No fetch was spent this round, on the ground that round 68 established there is no document to read: the Bank of Eritrea serves no governance, board, management or biography page, and Eritrea's three banks (Commercial Bank of Eritrea, Housing and Commerce Bank, Eritrean Investment and Development Bank) publish no board biographies, so the fallback route of a privately owned bank publishing a board page does not exist. All three Eritrean banks are state-owned in any event, so even a found career would be a public move and would not count on this row. There is nothing for a future round to open, and continuing to list ERI as a revolving-door target costs a budget line every round for a country with no source.

TKM: unchanged, and the recommendation stands - reclassify as structurally closed rather than leave it as a target. No fetch was spent this round. Round 68 searched in English and in Russian for the Central Bank of Turkmenistan's chairman, board and management pages and found no career list of any kind: the bank publishes no governor, board or management biographies, and the one biography that exists, centralbanking.com's 'Biography of newly-appointed Turkmen c bank chief' of 9 May 2002 on Ymamdurdy Gandymow, truncates at a paywall before naming a single employer. Every Turkmen bank is state-owned, so a found career would be a public move and would not count on this row even if a career list appeared. Two rounds of searching plus this one agree; the row should record TKM as structurally closed.

The twelve depth codes (DEU FRA ITA ESP NLD BEL AUT PRT GRC IRL CHE SWE) and the four closed codes (BRN DJI ERI TKM) were each read in have_rd.json before any search; every existing record for all twelve was listed and compared on person, episode and source URL before a candidate was accepted. One near-miss belonging to another country was found and NOT filed: round 68's Brunei note records a Baiduri Bank executive whose central bank was Bank Negara Malaysia, which belongs to MYS and is already held there - checked in have_rd.json and left alone.
leads_not_opened: BEL: a document stating Banque Lambert's ownership (Lambert family or Groupe Bruxelles Lambert structure page) would convert the Jean Godeaux record, whose career half is already confirmed from the National Bank of Belgium's own 2009 press release.

DEU: Andreas Dombret (Bundesbank Executive Board 2010-2018, previously vice-chairman for Europe at Bank of America and at Rothschild, afterwards senior adviser at Houlihan Lokey) needs an institutional CV from an employer or the bank, not a speaker page.
AUT: board and supervisory-board biographies at Erste Group, Raiffeisen Bank International, BAWAG and Oberbank - the OeNB itself publishes no careers.
PRT: the board CV PDFs that Millennium bcp and Novo Banco publish for their own directors, searched for Banco de Portugal service with dates.
GRC: the Bank of Greece's own past-governor and past-deputy-governor pages, and the board biographies of Alpha Bank, Eurobank and National Bank of Greece.

CHE: the Swiss National Bank publishes a numbered series of short biographies for every past Governing Board member at https://www.snb.ch/en/the-snb/organisation/history/short-biographies, each a separate PDF with a dated 'Professional career' and 'Board positions' list. One of them (Gehrig) converted this round on a single fetch. This is the richest single career-list resource found on this row and the series has not been read through; a future round could take several Swiss records from it cheaply, and the same index names the men who preceded him.

SWE: the Riksbank publishes the same per-member CV PDFs for every Executive Board member at /globalassets/media/riksbanken/direktionen/cv/ - Lars Nyberg (deputy governor 1999-2011, previously at Swedbank and Nordbanken) is the obvious next one.
NLD: De Nederlandsche Bank's other executive directors have CVs published by the EBA and the ECB Supervisory Board in the same series as the Sijbrand CV used here.
